what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 2: Two records tilted off the lean in the ordered odds: what each does to the other, and to where records form. SETTING (possibility's odds under the owner's reading: records move, one per site at a time; possibility shifts at the site as the neighbourhood changes; block 42's reading that an unformed site's odds are a condition for its neighbours, pi_x(s) ~ prod_y (K1 pi_y)(s), a record a point mass; open PRs #8919 (block 103: possibility's odds on the sphere menu - past the massless point beta0 in (5085, 5086)/10^4 the turn of the lean has per-neighbour eigenvalue exactly 1/6, fed by content off the lean (beta s_perp.s0_perp), never by a count; bodies charge it by capacity; vacancies at the neutral scale), #8548 (block 42: the reading; T4(b) the content-blind normalizer; T5 seven outcomes; T6 boundary values), #8547 (block 41: T4 the symmetry lemma and its quadratic two-tilt model), #8153 (block 19: the sphere menu), #8546 (block 40: the neutral scale), #8866 (block 96: waves need a coupling time reversal flips); decision record #8572 (seventeenth addendum); ALL clauses supplied, nothing adopted; read the notes on their PR branches before starting - git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). TASK: block 103 T3-T4: in the ordered sea (beta > beta0) a record of content s0 feeds the turn channel beta s_perp.s0_perp at first order; held as a boundary value it makes the transverse lean u0 h_S (h_S the walk's reaching probability). Block 42 T4(b): a content-blind weight (the normalizer <prod_y g_y> of a site, which any formation clause weighing a record of unread content uses) sees the leans only at second order. (a) Exactly at second order in the turn field: the normalizer of an unformed site at distance r from ONE tilted record, its law in r on Z^3 and its sign (is formation favoured or disfavoured near a tilted record?). (b) For TWO tilted records at separation d with transverse contents a, b: the part of the configuration's content-averaged weight (block 42 T4(b)'s normalizer, summed or multiplied over sites as you justify) that depends on d and on a.b; its sign for like (a.b > 0) and unlike tilts and its law in d, against block 41 T4's quadratic model -kappa ab G(r)/(G(0)^2 - G(r)^2) (like attract). (c) The two-record field in the linear channel as a boundary-value problem: when it is the superposition of one-record fields and when not. probes/lib/odds_sphere_lattice.py solves the nonlinear odds with any held records (a first run with two like records at distance 2 on 13^3 shows the site weight raised between them and lowered around them). HIT: (a) or (b) exact at the stated order. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/odds-two-tilted-records/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/odds-two-tilted-records/<name>/check.py"
